idea: Independent second opinion on an investment thesis
buyer: PMs and family office CIOs about to size a position
pain: No independent challenge before committing capital
v1: Fixed-fee red-team memo on a thesis they send
verdict: Lovely fit and instantly sellable, but the purchase is occasional and the price low.

why.distribution: Her exact peer group, and the ask is small and easy to trial.
why.demand: Inferred from her own experience of wanting challenge; nobody currently buys this as a product.
why.fmf: Generalist coverage is precisely the skill - fast, credible challenge on an unfamiliar name.
why.revenue_structure: Occasional one-off purchases with no rhythm.
why.defensibility: Any credible ex-analyst can offer the same thing.
why.time_to_revenue: Could be sold within a fortnight.
why.tailwind: Flat; nothing structural pushes funds toward buying external challenge.
why.ceiling: £4k x 25 = £100k, and 25 red-team memos requires a habit that does not yet exist anywhere.

ceiling_arithmetic: £4k x 25 memos = £100k. The binding problem is frequency: a PM might want this twice a year, so 25 memos needs 12+ regular clients in a category nobody currently budgets for.
carries: Delightful fit and near-zero friction to trial.
kills: There is no budget line for it, and no natural repeat rhythm.
test: Offer it free once to two PMs, then quote £4k for the second.
test_fail: They loved the free one and never came back.
